content.prompt: The rise and fall of the tide at a harbour can be modelled by the function $y=7+3\cos\left(\frac{4\pi t}{25}\right)$, where $y$ is the water depth in metres and $t$ is the number of hours after the first high tide at 2 am.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How long, in hours, is the time between successive high tides?

answer.worked: $$\color{#268cff}\begin{aligned}\text{Period}&=\frac{2\pi}{a}\\&=\frac{2\pi}{\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}\right)}\\&=12.5\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Sketch the graph for one cycle.

answer.worked: The mean depth is $7$ m, the amplitude is $3$ m and the period is $12.5$ hours. The curve starts at its maximum, reaches its minimum halfway through the cycle, and returns to its maximum.

spec.description: One complete cosine cycle, with a short continuation arrow at the right end; positive arrowed axes, source tick labels and no grid or origin label. Ordinary axes and labels use black; the teaching solution curve uses house blue.
spec.mathematics: y=7+3 cos(4πt/25); maximum 10 at t=0 and 12.5; minimum 4 at t=6.25; period 12.5.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the lowest level of water in the harbour, and at what time does this occur?

answer.worked:
The lowest position occurs when $\cos\left(\frac{4\pi t}{25}\right)=-1$.
$$\color{#268cff}\begin{aligned}y_{\min}&=7-3\\&=4\text{ m}\\\frac{4\pi t}{25}&=\pi\\t&=\frac{25}{4}\\&=6.25\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$$
This is 6 hours 15 minutes after 2 am, so the lowest depth is $4$ m at 8:15 am.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A bridge obstructs a ship’s exit from the harbour. The ship can only leave if the water depth is 8.5 m or less. When is the earliest the ship can leave, to the nearest minute?

answer.worked:
$$\color{#268cff}\begin{aligned}8.5&=7+3\cos\left(\frac{4\pi t}{25}\right)\\3\cos\left(\frac{4\pi t}{25}\right)&=1.5\\\cos\left(\frac{4\pi t}{25}\right)&=\frac12\\\frac{4\pi t}{25}&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\t&=\frac{25}{12}\text{ hours}\\&=2\text{ hours }5\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$
The depth decreases from the high tide, so this first crossing is the earliest time the ship can leave. Two hours five minutes after 2 am is 4:05 am.

content.prompt: The depth of water, $d$ metres, in a bay is modelled by $d=k\cos(at)+c$, where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight. In each case, find the values of $k$, $a$ and $c$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: High tide of 2.9 metres occurs at 5 am and the next low tide of 0.5 metres occurs at 10 am.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amplitude}&=\frac{2.9-0.5}{2}=1.2\\c&=\frac{2.9+0.5}{2}=1.7\\\text{Period}&=2\times5=10\\a&=\frac{2\pi}{10}=\frac{\pi}{5}\end{align*}$$
At $t=5$, $\cos\pi=-1$, but the depth is a maximum, so $k=-1.2$.

Check: $d(5)=-1.2(-1)+1.7=2.9$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Low tide of 1.1 metres occurs at 3 am and the next high tide of 3.5 metres occurs at 6 am.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amplitude}&=\frac{3.5-1.1}{2}=1.2\\c&=\frac{3.5+1.1}{2}=2.3\\\text{Period}&=2\times3=6\\a&=\frac{2\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}\end{align*}$$
At $t=3$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the depth is a minimum, so $k=1.2$.

Check: $d(3)=1.2(-1)+2.3=1.1$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: High tide of 4.6 metres occurs at 7 am, and the low tide is 1.8 metres. There are 14 hours between successive high tides.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amplitude}&=\frac{4.6-1.8}{2}=1.4\\c&=\frac{4.6+1.8}{2}=3.2\\\text{Period}&=14\\a&=\frac{2\pi}{14}=\frac{\pi}{7}\end{align*}$$
At $t=7$, $\cos\pi=-1$, but the depth is a maximum, so $k=-1.4$.

Check: $d(7)=-1.4(-1)+3.2=4.6$.

content.prompt: Scientists monitoring a population of penguins on Heard Island found that the number of penguins varies between a high of 900 at the start of the year and a low of 700 on 30 June and is approximated by the cosine function $P(t)=k\cos at+c$, where $t$ is the number of months since the start of the year, and $k$, $a$ and $c$ are constants.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch a graph of the penguin population over a whole year.

answer.worked: The maximum is 900 at $t=0$ and the minimum is 700 at $t=6$, so the half-period is 6 months and the period is 12 months. The mean population is $\frac{900+700}{2}=800$. Sketch one cosine cycle, starting and ending at 900, with its minimum at $(6,700)$.

spec.description: One cosine cycle with monthly ticks 1–12, vertical ticks 600–1000, an axis break below 600 and an arrow at the curve endpoint. Axes and labels use house black; the population curve uses standard blue.
spec.mathematics: P(t)=100 cos(pi t/6)+800 for 0<=t<=12. Drawing coordinates use y=(P-600)/100+0.5 above the vertical-axis break.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the values of $k$, $a$ and $c$ for the function.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}k&=\frac{900-700}{2}\\k&=100\\c&=\frac{900+700}{2}\\c&=800\end{align*}$$
Half-period $=6$ months, so period $=12$ months.
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{2\pi}{12}\\a&=\frac{\pi}{6}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: According to the population function, how many penguins will there be on the island on 31 March?

answer.worked:
On 31 March, $t=3$.
$$\begin{align*}P(3)&=100\cos\left(\frac{\pi(3)}{6}\right)+800\\P(3)&=100\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+800\\P(3)&=800\end{align*}$$
There will be 800 penguins.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}x(0)&=2\cos(0)+8\\&=10\text{ metres}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How deep is the bay at low tide?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}x(7)&=2\cos\pi+8\\&=6\text{ metres}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: When did the first low tide after 7 am occur?

children.label: b
children.prompt: If it has a frequency of $50$ Hz (meaning $50$ cycles per second), find the value of $a$.

answer.worked:
The frequency is $50$ Hz, so the period is $\frac{1}{50}$ s.

answer.worked:
Substituting $k=240$, $a=100\pi$ and $c=0$ gives
$$V(t)=240\sin(100\pi t).$$

content.prompt:
A set of tidal waves has a maximum height of 20 m and a minimum height of 6 m.
The waves break every 10 seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the equation of a sine function $y=k\sin(at)+c$ that describes the wave motion.

answer.short: $y=7\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)+13$, where $t$ is in seconds and $y$ is in metres.
answer.worked:
Mean position: $c=\frac{20+6}{2}=13$ m.

Amplitude: $k=\frac{20-6}{2}=7$ m.

The period is 10 s, so $a=\frac{2\pi}{10}=\frac{\pi}{5}$.

$$y=7\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)+13.$$
Here $t$ is in seconds and $y$ is in metres.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the first 4 times that the waves reach their maximum height.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}20&=7\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)+13\\\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)&=1\\\frac{\pi t}{5}&=\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{2},\frac{9\pi}{2},\frac{13\pi}{2}\\t&=2.5,12.5,22.5,32.5\text{ seconds}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the first time that the waves reach their minimum height.

answer.worked:
The minimum occurs when $\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)=-1$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\pi t}{5}&=\frac{3\pi}{2}\\t&=7.5\text{ seconds}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: When will the height of the waves be in the centre?

answer.worked:
The centre height is the mean position, 13 m, reached when $\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)=0$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\pi t}{5}&=0,\pi,2\pi,3\pi,4\pi,5\pi,\ldots\\t&=0,5,10,15,20,25,\ldots\text{ seconds}.\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: The height of the water, $h$ metres, in a bay varies over time and can be modelled by a cosine function of the form $h(t)=k\cos(at)+c$, where $k$, $a$ and $c$ are constants and $t$ represents the number of hours after midnight. On a particular day off the coast of South Australia, a high tide of 4.5 metres occurred at 6:00 am and a low tide of 0.5 metre occurred at 12:00 pm.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Determine a model for the height, $h$ metres, of the water as a function of time, $t$ hours, since midnight by finding the values of $k$, $a$ and $c$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amplitude}&=\frac{4.5-0.5}{2}\\\text{Amplitude}&=2\\c&=\frac{4.5+0.5}{2}\\c&=2.5\end{align*}$$
The time from high tide to low tide is 6 hours, so the period is 12 hours.
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{2\pi}{12}\\a&=\frac{\pi}{6}\end{align*}$$
At $t=6$, $\cos\left(\frac{\pi\times6}{6}\right)=-1$. Since this is high tide,
$$\begin{align*}4.5&=-k+2.5\\k&=-2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence write the rule of $h(t)$.

answer.worked:
Substituting $k=-2$, $a=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $c=2.5$ gives
$$h(t)=-2\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)+2.5.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: At what time does the second high tide occur?

answer.worked: Successive high tides are 12 hours apart. The second high tide occurs 12 hours after 6:00 am, at 6:00 pm.

content.prompt:
A Ferris wheel with a radius of 35 m rotates once every 90 seconds. Passengers enter a cabin at the loading point, which is 2 m above level ground.

The height, $h(t)$ metres, above the ground is given by $h(t)=-35\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{45}\right)+37$, where $t$ seconds is the time after leaving the lowest level.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the graph of $h(t)$ for a 3-minute period after a cabin passes the loading point and state the coordinates of the $h$ intercept.

answer.short: Translate the inside-temperature graph 3 hours to the left to obtain the outside-temperature graph.
answer.worked:
The replacement of $t$ by $t+3$ shifts the graph 3 hours to the left. The outside temperature reaches its maximum of $35^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at $t=3$, while the inside temperature reaches its maximum at $t=6$.

On $0\leq t\leq12$, the outside graph passes through $(0,20+15\sqrt2/2)$, $(3,35)$, $(9,20)$ and $(12,20-15\sqrt2/2)$. Draw it on the same axes as the inside graph.

children.label: g
children.prompt: When are the temperatures the same and what temperature is this? Give the temperature to 2 decimal places.

answer.short: At $t=4.5$, or 1:30 pm; both temperatures are approximately $33.86^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
answer.worked:
Graphically, the inside temperature peaks at $t=6$ and the outside temperature peaks at $t=3$. Between these peaks, the outside temperature decreases while the inside temperature increases. The identical curves are symmetric about their respective peaks, so they have equal temperatures halfway between the peaks:
$$t=\frac{3+6}{2}=4.5.$$
$$\begin{aligned}T(4.5)&=15\sin\left(\frac{\pi(4.5)}{12}\right)+20\\&=15\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{8}\right)+20\\&\approx33.86^{\circ}\mathrm{C}.\end{aligned}$$
This occurs at 1:30 pm.

Alternatively, set the two models equal:
$$\begin{aligned}15\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{12}\right)+20&=15\sin\left(\frac{\pi(t+3)}{12}\right)+20,\\\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{12}\right)&=\sin\left(\frac{\pi(t+3)}{12}\right).\end{aligned}$$
For $\sin X=\sin Y$, the possibilities are $X=Y+2n\pi$ or $X=\pi-Y+2n\pi$, where $n$ is an integer. The first case is impossible here because the arguments differ by $\pi/4$. The second gives
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi t}{12}&=\pi-\frac{\pi(t+3)}{12}+2n\pi,\\t&=4.5+12n.\end{aligned}$$
Only $t=4.5$ lies in $0\leq t\leq12$.

answer.worked:

$$\begin{align*}-25\cos\theta+27&>40\\-25\cos\theta&>13\\\cos\theta&<-0.52\end{align*}$$

$$0.8230<\theta<1.6911$$

content.prompt: A sound wave can be modelled using a function $P(t)=k \sin at$, where $P$ is air pressure in Pascals, $t$ is time in milliseconds (ms) and $k$ and $a$ are constants.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write the equation for a sound wave $P_1(t)$ that has an amplitude of $2$ Pascals and a period of $5$ ms.

answer.worked:
The amplitude is $2$, so $k=2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Period}&=\frac{2\pi}{a}=5\\a&=\frac{2\pi}{5}\end{align*}$$
$$P_1(t)=2\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}t\right)$$

children.label: b
children.prompt:
The graph of $P_1(t)$ from part a is shown.
On the diagram, sketch the graph of $P_2(t)=4 \sin(\frac{\pi}{10}t)$ for $0 \leq t \leq 10$.

answer.short: A sine wave of amplitude $4$ and period $20$: half a wave from $(0,0)$ up to the peak $(5,4)$ and back to $(10,0)$.
answer.worked:
For $P_2(t)=4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{10}t\right)$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amplitude}&=4\\\text{Period}&=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/10}=20\end{align*}$$
Over $0\le t\le10$ the graph is half of one wave. It starts at $(0,0)$, reaches its maximum a quarter of a period later at $(5,4)$, and returns to the axis at $(10,0)$.

The sketch of $P_2$ is shown with $P_1$ in the solution diagram.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence, find the values of $t$, where $0 < t < 10$, for which functions $P_1(t)$ and $P_2(t)$ are BOTH decreasing.

answer.worked:
From the graph of $P_2$, the function is decreasing from its peak at $t=5$ to $t=10$, so on $5<t<10$.

From the graph of $P_1$ (period $5$), it is decreasing from each peak to the next trough. The peaks are at $t=1.25$ and $t=6.25$ and the troughs are at $t=3.75$ and $t=8.75$. So $P_1$ is decreasing on $1.25<t<3.75$ and on $6.25<t<8.75$.

Both are decreasing where these intervals overlap:
$$6.25<t<8.75$$

content.prompt:
Anna is sitting in a carriage of a Ferris wheel which is revolving. The height, $A(t)$, in metres above the ground of the top of her carriage is given by
$$A(t)=c-k\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{24}\right),$$
where $t$ is the time in seconds after Anna's carriage first reaches the bottom of its revolution and $c$ and $k$ are constants.

The top of a carriage reaches a greatest height of 39 metres and a lowest height of 3 metres.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the value of $c$ and $k$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many seconds does it take for one complete revolution of the Ferris wheel?

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Period}&=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/24}\\&=48\text{ seconds}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Billie is in another carriage. The height, $B(t)$, in metres above the ground of the top of her carriage is given by
$$B(t)=c-k\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{24}(t-6)\right),$$
where $c$ and $k$ are as found in part a.

During each revolution, there are two occasions when Anna's and Billie's carriages are at the same heights. At what two heights does this occur? Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
A sketch shows that the two height graphs have a phase shift of 6 seconds. Their equal-height points lie halfway between their corresponding troughs and halfway between their corresponding peaks.

Anna's trough is at $t=0$ and Billie's is at $t=6$, so the first common height occurs at $t=3$. Anna's peak is at $t=24$ and Billie's is at $t=30$, so the second occurs at $t=27$.
$$\begin{aligned}A(3)&=21-18\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{24}\right)\\&=21-18\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)\\&\approx4.37\text{ m}\\A(27)&=21-18\cos\left(\frac{27\pi}{24}\right)\\&=21-18\cos\left(\frac{9\pi}{8}\right)\\&\approx37.63\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
Check: $B(3)=21-18\cos(-\pi/8)\approx4.37$ and $B(27)=21-18\cos(7\pi/8)\approx37.63$.

The two heights are 4.37 metres and 37.63 metres.

content.prompt:
A particle is moving in a straight line and is oscillating backwards and forwards.
At time $t$ seconds, it has displacement $x$ metres from a fixed point $O$ on the line, where
$$x=A\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}t+\alpha\right),\quad A>0,\quad 0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
After $1$ second the particle is $2$ metres to the right of $O$, and after $3$ seconds it is $4$ metres to the left of $O$.
Given that $A\cos\alpha-A\sin\alpha=2\sqrt{2}$ and $A\cos\alpha+A\sin\alpha=4\sqrt{2}$:

children.label: a
children.prompt: Solve the equations simultaneously, to find the values of $A$ and $\alpha$ in exact form.

answer.worked:
Adding the two equations:
$$\begin{align*}2A\cos\alpha&=6\sqrt{2}\\A\cos\alpha&=3\sqrt{2}\end{align*}$$
Subtracting the first equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}2A\sin\alpha&=2\sqrt{2}\\A\sin\alpha&=\sqrt{2}\end{align*}$$
Squaring and adding:
$$\begin{align*}A^2(\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha)&=(3\sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{2})^2\\A^2&=20\\A&=2\sqrt{5}\quad(A>0)\end{align*}$$
Dividing:
$$\tan\alpha=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{3}$$
Since $0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the particle first passes through $O$ after $\frac{4}{\pi}\tan^{-1}3$ seconds.

answer.worked:
The particle is at $O$ when $x=0$:
$$A\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}t+\alpha\right)=0\implies\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}t+\alpha\right)=0$$
At $t=0$, $\frac{\pi}{4}t+\alpha=\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$, and the argument increases with $t$. So the first time $t>0$ that the cosine is zero is when the argument equals $\frac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\pi}{4}t+\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{2}\\\frac{\pi}{4}t&=\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$$
In a right-angled triangle with an angle $\theta$ where $\tan\theta=\frac{1}{3}$, the other acute angle is $\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta$ and its tangent is $3$. So $\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3}=\tan^{-1}3$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\pi}{4}t&=\tan^{-1}3\\t&=\frac{4}{\pi}\tan^{-1}3\end{align*}$$
Therefore the particle first passes through $O$ after $\frac{4}{\pi}\tan^{-1}3$ seconds.

content.prompt:
The population of wombats in a particular location varies according to the rule
$$n(t)=1200+400\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)$$
where $n$ is the number of wombats and $t$ is the number of months after 1 March 2018.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the period and amplitude of the function $n$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}T&=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/3}\\&=6\text{ months}\end{align*}$$
Amplitude: $400$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the maximum and minimum populations of wombats in this location.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Maximum}&=1200+400\\&=1600\text{ wombats}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Minimum}&=1200-400\\&=800\text{ wombats}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find $n(10)$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}n(10)&=1200+400\cos\left(\frac{10\pi}{3}\right)\\&=1200+400\left(-\frac12\right)\\&=1000\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Over the 12 months from 1 March 2018, find the fraction of time when the population of wombats in this location was less than $n(10)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}1200+400\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)&<1000\\\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)&<-\frac12\end{align*}$$
The boundary times in the first cycle satisfy
$$\begin{align*}\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)&=-\frac12\\\frac{\pi t}{3}&=\frac{2\pi}{3},\ \frac{4\pi}{3}\\t&=2,\ 4.\end{align*}$$
Using the period of $6$ months, the other boundary times in the domain are $t=8$ and $t=10$. The population is below $1000$ for $2<t<4$ and $8<t<10$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total time}&=(4-2)+(10-8)\\&=4\text{ months}\\\text{Fraction of time}&=\frac4{12}\\&=\frac13\end{align*}$$
A sketch is useful here for solving the inequality.
